scenes.headline: Compaction
scenes.subtitle: Merge small files into large, efficient ones
scenes.narration: Compaction consolidates many small Delta files into fewer large files to restore query performance.

scenes.headline: The small files problem
items: Streaming and frequent appends create tiny files
Each file adds open, list, and metadata overhead
Queries slow down as file counts explode
scenes.narration: Micro-batch writes and streaming steadily produce many small files. Every file costs time to open and adds metadata overhead. Left unchecked, this file sprawl cripples query performance.

scenes.headline: Compacting with OPTIMIZE
scenes.narration: OPTIMIZE bin-packs the many small files into larger, more efficient ones. Adding ZORDER also co-locates related rows during the same rewrite. The table now serves reads with far less file overhead.

scenes.headline: Compaction lifecycle
scenes.narration: As ingestion continues, the number of small files climbs. Running OPTIMIZE rewrites them into a compact set. Query engines then scan fewer, larger files with better throughput.

scenes.headline: Best practices
items: Schedule OPTIMIZE regularly on hot tables
Use auto-compaction and optimized writes for streaming
Run VACUUM to clean up obsolete files
scenes.narration: Regular compaction keeps performance stable on actively written tables. Databricks auto-optimize features can compact automatically during writes. Pairing with VACUUM removes stale files and controls storage cost.

scenes.text: Many small files are the silent tax on Delta performance; compaction pays it off.
scenes.narration: Healthy Delta tables keep files large and counts low, so scans stay fast.
